questions: Does slalom progress rise above 0.76, and do slalom finishes rise above 6/20? Report slalom completion_time for any finish.
Does slalom line_loss_events fall toward 1.0 from 1.10? Report the heading and speed at first line loss if it stays at 1.1 or more.
Does s-bend steering_oscillation stay under 0.35, and does the s-bend hold 19/20 or better?
Does the oval hold 20/20 at about 1.9 to 2.0 s?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses any trial, or the score falls below 785.3, return body_length to 0.12 m with mass 0.45 kg. If slalom progress rises but line loss stays at 1.1 or more, keep geometry fixed and report the entry heading and speed so the controller entry speed can be the next lever.

intent: Keep the iteration 10 design (best so far, 785.3) and change only body_length from 0.12 m to 0.11 m. This lowers yaw inertia by about 8 percent at unchanged mass, so the slalom's direction changes are taken faster without changing acceleration or rolling resistance. Sensing (seven 12 mm sensors, ±0.036 m span, 0.012 m pitch, lead 0.06 m), wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m and body_width 0.12 m stay fixed. The Integrator should keep the iteration 10 controller gains so the race isolates body_length.
learning: Iterations 7 to 10 show that lowering yaw inertia (mass 0.7 to 0.45 kg, body_length 0.16 to 0.12 m) raised slalom progress from 0.30 to 0.76 and finishes from 0 to 6/20, while the s-bend and oval held. Narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m (iteration 8) added s-bend jitter without a slalom gain, so track stays at 0.10 m. Iteration 11 tests whether yaw inertia can be reduced further through body_length alone, keeping mass fixed.
rationale: Iteration 10 (mass 0.45 kg, body_length 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, seven 12 mm sensors at x = ±0.036 m, y = 0.06 m) is the best design so far at 785.3, up from 741.9. The oval held 20/20 at 1.97 s and the s-bend held 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.277, well under the 0.35 limit. The slalom improved again: mean progress rose from 0.68 to 0.76, finishes rose from 2/20 to 6/20, and line_loss_events fell only slightly, from 1.15 to 1.10. Yaw inertia is the only geometry lever that has moved the slalom in three consecutive steps (0.7 to 0.6 to 0.5 to 0.45 kg). Mass is now near its 0.4 kg lower bound. Rather than cut mass further, I reduce yaw inertia through body_length, which the contract says has no direct effect on dynamics apart from yaw inertia. Body_length 0.12 m to 0.11 m gives I = 0.45*(0.0121+0.0144)/12 ≈ 0.00100 kg·m², about 8 percent below the current 0.00108. This is a smaller step than the last mass changes, to limit overshoot risk, since line loss is still about 1.1. body_width stays at 0.12 m, so the off-track limit is unchanged. Expected: slalom progress above 0.76, more finishes, and line_loss_events toward 1.0, with the oval at 20/20 and the s-bend at 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation under 0.35. Fallback: if s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses any trial, or the score falls below 785.3, return body_length to 0.12 m with mass 0.45 kg, the best measured design.
